summary: Backend-only verification of the NEW direct-Stripe subscription integration (migrated off emergentintegrations.payments.stripe → standard `stripe` Python SDK on user's OWN Stripe account). 19/19 pytest cases passed against the public preview URL with ZERO code changes required. Coverage: (1) GET /api/subscription/plans — both plans present, monthly $3.99/usd/month, annual $36.99/usd/year with savings_label, stripe_price_id correctly stripped from public payload, free_tier_limits dict included; (2) GET /api/subscription/status — no-auth → is_premium=false + all features false + subscription_status='free'; admin auth → is_premium=true + all features true + expires_at + plan_id; (3) POST /api/subscription/create-checkout — 401 unauthenticated, 400 on invalid plan_id, both plans return REAL Stripe URLs (https://checkout.stripe.com/...) and cs_test_... session IDs, payment_transactions row inserted with payment_status='pending' (verified directly in MongoDB); (4) GET /api/subscription/checkout-status/{id} — 404 on unknown id, known just-created session returns 200 with full shape {status, payment_status, amount_total, currency}, payment_status='unpaid' for unpaid session, NO 500s; (5) POST /api/webhook/stripe dev-fallback path (STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET blank) — accepts events without signature verification, checkout.session.completed correctly sets is_premium=true + plan_id=premium_annual + expires_at on admin user, customer.subscription.updated with status='active' + current_period_end syncs subscription_status='active' + new expires_at, customer.subscription.deleted flips is_premium=false; all webhook calls return 200 {received: true}; (6) /api/user/feature-access/oracle_readings_unlimited returns has_access=true for admin (after restoring premium); (7) Regression smoke: /api/spirit-guides/familiarity, /api/daily/card, /api/companion-guide all 200 with admin auth. Backend-only scope — no React Native or design checks performed.

minor.issue: Dev-mode fallback (STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET blank) is working as intended and emits a loud WARNING log. This is acceptable for the current pre-production state, but MUST be hardened before going live — once the user creates the webhook endpoint in their Stripe dashboard and provides a whsec_, populate STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET and the code will automatically switch to signature-verified mode (no code change needed).

Idempotency key includes a random uuid4() suffix (etheria_checkout_{user_id}_{plan_id}_{rand}) which makes every call a new key — so Stripe will NOT dedupe back-to-back retries. If the goal of the idempotency key is true dedupe, drop the uuid suffix (or use a stable hash of the request). Currently each test run creates a fresh cs_test_... session, which is the actual observed behavior.

When the underlying transaction has payment_status='paid' (cached), the endpoint returns {status:'complete', payment_status:'paid', already_processed:true} — but does NOT include amount_total/currency in that branch. Clients that always expect amount_total/currency in the response will break on the cached path. Minor — only matters if frontend re-polls after success.

action_items: (Production hardening) Once the user creates the Stripe webhook endpoint in their dashboard and obtains a whsec_..., populate STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET in /app/backend/.env — the code already auto-switches to signature-verified mode when the var is non-empty, no code change required.

(Optional) In routes/subscription.py create_checkout_session, drop the uuid4().hex[:8] suffix from idem_key (or replace with a deterministic hash of plan_id + user_id + minute-bucket) so Stripe can actually dedupe retried calls. Today every call gets a unique key.

(Optional) In routes/subscription.py get_checkout_status, when returning the cached-paid branch (line ~314), also include amount_total/currency from the stored transaction so the response shape is consistent across cached and live paths.
(Optional) Consider exposing the plan's `stripe_price_id` is correctly stripped — verified server-side. No frontend change needed.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/subscription.py is 582 lines — under the 700-line limit, single-responsibility (one router file for /subscription, /webhook, /user/feature-access). Good separation.

Webhook dev-fallback path (lines 387-393) is explicit and well-logged with a loud WARNING. Acceptable for the pre-production phase. Production will auto-harden once STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is populated.

Excellent defensive handling around timezone-aware/naive datetime comparison in /subscription/status (lines 201-209) and check_feature_access (lines 556-564) — mirror of the bug we fixed in iteration_2 for companion.py. Good consistency.
Webhook handler catches all exceptions and returns 200 (lines 411-414) — correct pattern. Prevents Stripe from infinitely retrying on a transient handler bug.

_handle_subscription_change correctly falls back to looking up user by stripe_customer_id when metadata.user_id is missing (lines 460-465). This is critical for the customer.subscription.updated/deleted events that Stripe sometimes sends without preserving metadata.
MongoDB _id is correctly excluded by always projecting individual fields or using $set on existing docs. No leakage observed.
All HTTP status codes are appropriate (400 invalid plan, 401 unauth, 404 unknown session, 502 upstream Stripe failure, 500 only when Stripe isn't configured at boot).
Pydantic models (CreateCheckoutRequest, SubscriptionStatusResponse) properly typed. plan_id defaults to premium_monthly which is sensible.
Stripe SDK is correctly initialized at module load (stripe.api_key = os.environ.get(...)) — happens after dotenv has loaded because server.py loads env before importing routes.
MINOR: success_url uses double-braces `{{CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}}` which Stripe will substitute — correct Stripe convention. Verified in actual response URL.
MINOR: SUBSCRIPTION_PLANS is a module-level dict — fine as a single source of truth. If you ever add a third plan, also update INTERVAL_TO_DAYS if it has a new interval (e.g., 'week').
Idempotency key drift noted in minor issues above — not security-critical but defeats Stripe's dedupe.
